title: Why Countries Are Talking About Their Stored Diesel
summary:
A fuel decision in one country can affect prices far away. That is why the United States and European countries are discussing diesel, a fuel used by truckers, farmers and other businesses.

President Donald Trump has threatened to stop American diesel exports, meaning sales to other countries. He also said he may ask European countries to release some of the diesel they keep in reserve. These are possible steps; no export ban has been announced in this report.

Why does it matter? The United States sells between 1.2 million and 1.5 million barrels of diesel abroad each day. Britain gets a significant amount of diesel from America, while most American exports go to Latin America.

Keeping more diesel in the United States could lower prices there. But experts warn that other countries could face higher prices unless they find more supplies.

War has already disrupted supplies. British diesel prices reached record highs this week, according to the BBC.

British and European officials are discussing what to do. Britain's government says there is no reason to worry about shortages, although prices could rise further.
why_it_matters: Changes to diesel supplies could affect fuel prices for drivers, farmers and businesses in several countries.
